title: Quashing of FIR - when High Courts actually intervene
p1:
Can an FIR be cancelled even after the police start investigating?

Many people think once an FIR is registered, the case must go to trial. That is not always true.
p2: A High Court can step in and quash an FIR when continuing the case would be an abuse of the legal process. For example, if the allegations do not reveal any offence, the complaint is clearly baseless, or the dispute is purely personal but given a criminal colour.
p3:
But High Courts do not act like trial courts and decide who is guilty or innocent. Their role is to prevent misuse of criminal law when the facts themselves show that prosecution should not continue.

A surprising point: even a genuine-looking FIR can sometimes be quashed if the legal requirements of the alleged offence are not met.
conclusion: Should courts have wider powers to stop cases that appear to misuse criminal law, or could that risk affecting genuine complaints?
